newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Gujral says selective on foreign investors.
newsitem.headline: India's Gujral says selective on foreign investors.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Saturday he preferred to be selective towards foreign investment with a preference for infrastructure, but added he would not object to any foreign investor.

"Selective not in the sense of standing in the way of something. But India has to have its own agenda of growth and also a clear agenda of emphasis," Gujral, responding to a question, told Reuters Television in an interview.

"We need more investment in all infrastructure (areas). Energy, particularly," Gujral said. "We need more roads, better roads. We need to invest more in telecommunications. Any outside investments in this region, I will welcome them."

Gujral, who was sworn in earlier this week as prime minister to head a new centre-left coalition formed by the 15-party United Front, said his government would strive to protect India's interests without isolating its economy.
"If there is investment available to me for building a road, I would prefer that to getting an agenda for getting fried chicken," he said.
"It (the economy) has to safeguard Indian interests. It is not exclusivist. It is not narrow. We don't keep our doors shut but we must decide where our interests are," Gujral said.
